introduction_markdown:
This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: answer ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: answer ALL TWO questions in this section. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3; if you attempt more than 2 questions, only the first 2 will be considered. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, Na = 23.0, Cu = 64.0, Cl = 35.5, K = 39.0, N = 14.0, S = 32.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K.

questions.enonce_markdown:
You are expected to transfer 25 cm$^3$ of 0.1M $\mathrm{Na_2CO_{3(aq)}}$ into a conical flask and add 3 drops of the indicator. The solution is then titrated with dilute hydrochloric acid till the end point is reached

(i) Give a suitable indicator for the titration

(ii) What colour change will occur in the conical flask?

Initial colour ........ colour at the end point ........

(iii) The following table shows the results obtained by the student.

| Burette reading | Approximate | First accurate | Second accurate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Final reading | 25 cm$^3$ | 23.5 cm$^3$ | 23.3 cm$^3$ |
| Initial reading | 0.0 cm$^3$ | 0.0 cm$^3$ | 0.0 cm$^3$ |
| titre |  |  |  |

From the table above calculate the volume of the hydrochloric acid used

(iv) Calculate the concentration of the hydrochloric acid *[8 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Methyl orange** (a strong acid is added to a carbonate, so an indicator that changes in the acid range is suitable).

(ii) Initial colour: **yellow** (in the alkaline sodium carbonate); colour at the end point: **orange** (pink-red with a slight excess of acid).

(iii) Titre = final reading - initial reading:

| Burette reading | Approximate | First accurate | Second accurate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Final reading | 25.0 cm$^3$ | 23.5 cm$^3$ | 23.3 cm$^3$ |
| Initial reading | 0.0 cm$^3$ | 0.0 cm$^3$ | 0.0 cm$^3$ |
| titre | 25.0 cm$^3$ | 23.5 cm$^3$ | 23.3 cm$^3$ |

The approximate titre is only a trial and is not used. The two accurate titres agree within 0.2 cm$^3$, so the mean is used:

$\text{volume of HCl used} = \dfrac{23.5 + 23.3}{2} = 23.4\ \mathrm{cm^3}$

(iv) Equation: $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3} + 2\mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NaCl} + \mathrm{H_2O} + \mathrm{CO_2}$

Moles of $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$ $= 0.1 \times \dfrac{25}{1000} = 0.0025\ \mathrm{mol}$

From the equation, 1 mol of $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$ reacts with 2 mol of HCl, so moles of HCl $= 2 \times 0.0025 = 0.0050\ \mathrm{mol}$.

These moles are in $23.4\ \mathrm{cm^3} = 0.0234\ \mathrm{dm^3}$:

$[\mathrm{HCl}] = \dfrac{0.0050}{0.0234} = 0.2137 \approx 0.21\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}$

questions.enonce_markdown:
You are to prepare and collect dry samples of chlorine gas ($\mathrm{Cl_{2(g)}}$) and Ammonia gas ($\mathrm{NH_{3(g)}}$). Give a method that would be used for the collection of each gas

| Gases | Method |
|---|---|
| $\mathrm{Cl_{2(g)}}$ |  |
| $\mathrm{NH_{3(g)}}$ |  |

*[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Gases | Method |
|---|---|
| $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ | **Downward delivery** (upward displacement of air): chlorine is denser than air. It is first dried by passing it through concentrated sulphuric acid. |
| $\mathrm{NH_3}$ | **Upward delivery** (downward displacement of air): ammonia is less dense than air. It is first dried with quicklime, CaO. |

Neither gas can be collected over water because both dissolve very well in it, and a dry sample is required.

The following diagram is a section of an apparatus that was used to measure the temperature of a reaction mixture

![fig-4](gce-ol-chemistry-2022-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_4.png)

(i) Name the apparatus

(ii) Complete the following table

| Temperature after addition |  |
|---|---|
| Temperature before addition |  |
| Temperature change |  |

*[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) A **(laboratory) thermometer**.

(ii) The scale is read to 0.1 $^\circ$C (ten small divisions between two numbered marks). Before addition the mercury ends two small divisions below the 26 mark; after addition it ends just above the 33 mark.

| Temperature after addition | 33.1 $^\circ$C |
|---|---|
| Temperature before addition | 25.8 $^\circ$C |
| Temperature change | 7.3 $^\circ$C (a rise) |

Temperature change $= 33.1 - 25.8 = 7.3\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The temperature rises, so the reaction is exothermic.
